finding.claim: wipe() ignores the boolean returned by requireRole(), so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any caller that reaches the handler) calling POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id. No OWNER role is needed.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive wipe of the tenant's data.

trace.note: requireRole returns a boolean and does not throw (see its javadoc).
The return value is discarded, so execution continues whether or not the user has the role.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the ignored requireRole call. The sibling export() correctly uses checkRole, which throws, so the intent was clearly to enforce. No other middleware or auth exists in the repo, which contains only this file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole(u,"OWNER") at Admin.java:26 — returns boolean, doesn't throw, result discarded; no other auth in repo (only src/Admin.java exists). Sibling export() uses throwing checkRole (line 32).
verdict.reason: Admin.java:14-16 requireRole just returns a boolean and Admin.java:26 discards it, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any caller regardless of OWNER role (unlike checkRole at :32 which throws).

finding.claim: Role checks are not scoped to the tenant. The roles are a flat Set<String> and the tenant id from the URL is never compared to the caller. An OWNER of any tenant can export (and, once F1 is fixed, wipe) any other tenant's data. This is a cross-tenant IDOR. It is plausible rather than confirmed, because the user's tenant membership may be enforced upstream, outside this repo.
finding.source: An authenticated user holding the OWNER role in their own tenant, supplying another tenant's id in the {t} path segment.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) on line 33, and repo.wipe(tenant) on line 27.

trace.note: User has only a name and a role set. There is no tenant association.
checkRole tests only whether the role string is present, with no tenant context.
The attacker-supplied tenant is passed straight to the repo.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole enforces the role but not tenant ownership. No tenant-membership comparison exists on the path. Upstream middleware is not present in the repo, so I could not rule it out.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (Admin.java:18-22) throws on a missing role and is called as a bare statement at line 32, which is correct. It checks only the role and has no tenant context. No tenant-membership check exists anywhere in the repo. The only file mentioning "tenant" is Admin.java.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:4 gives User no tenant field, and checkRole (Admin.java:19) checks only the role string, so any OWNER can pass another tenant's id to repo.export at Admin.java:33. This holds for the code in the repo. Enforcement by upstream middleware outside the repo can't be ruled out.
